plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata (wild Boston fern)
plants.tip: The rootball must never dry out. Fronds that crisp from drought die back rather than greening up again.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Bostoniensis Compacta'
plants.tip: Compact enough for a shelf, but it wants the same steady moisture as a full-size Boston fern.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Bostoniensis Aurea'
plants.tip: Gold fronds scorch in direct sun. Bright indirect light holds the colour without burning the tips.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Fluffy Ruffles'
plants.tip: The dense upright fronds hide a fast-drying rootball. Check the compost every few days, not weekly.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Fluffy Duffy'
plants.tip: Small pots dry out fast. Stand it on a pebble tray rather than misting, which does little for humidity.
plants.colour: Bright green, finely cut and dense

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Rooseveltii'
plants.tip: Broad wavy fronds grow heavy and brittle. Cut spent fronds off at the base rather than trimming the tips.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Whitmanii'
plants.tip: Finely cut fronds shed constantly. Shake the plant out over a bin now and then rather than picking at it.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Whitmanii Improved'
plants.tip: Denser than the original, so water runs off the middle. Pour slowly at the rim, all the way round.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Dallas Jewel'
plants.tip: Bred to cope with drier rooms than most Boston ferns, but it still needs evenly damp compost.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Florida Ruffle'
plants.tip: Ruffled fronds trap dust. Rinse the whole plant under a tepid shower every few weeks.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Teddy Junior'
plants.tip: Compact and upright, so it hides a dry rootball well. Lift the pot; light means it needs water.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Emina'
plants.tip: Short stiff fronds sit close to the compost. Water at the edge so the crown does not stay wet.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Rita's Gold'
plants.tip: The chartreuse colour comes from light, not feed. In a dim corner it fades to ordinary green.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Tiger Fern'
plants.tip: Variegation reverts. Cut all-green fronds out at the base as they appear, or the plant turns plain.
plants.colour: Green with chartreuse to yellow streaks

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Green Lady'
plants.tip: Keep the compost evenly moist. A single full dry-out costs it an entire flush of fronds.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Green Fantasy'
plants.tip: Small enough for a terrarium, where the humidity suits it. In open air it needs water every few days.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Massii'
plants.tip: A drooping old cultivar for a hanging basket. Baskets dry fastest, so check it twice a week.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Verona'
plants.tip: Fine drooping fronds bruise easily. Site it where nothing brushes past it in daily use.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Smithii'
plants.tip: Very finely divided fronds lose water quickly. Never let the compost get past just-damp.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Suzi Wong' (cotton candy fern)
plants.tip: The lacy fronds mat together and shed. Thin the oldest fronds out at the base each spring.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Hillsii'
plants.tip: Crisped fronds hide the compost surface. Feel underneath them rather than judging moisture by eye.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Elegantissima'
plants.tip: An old crested cultivar. Remove browning fronds at the base; they never green up again.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Childsii'
plants.tip: Densely overlapping fronds keep the crown damp. Water round the rim, not into the middle.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Scottii'
plants.tip: Compact and upright, so it suits a shelf. Repot once the roots have formed a solid mat.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Norwoodii'
plants.tip: Doubly divided, curled fronds. Give it a quarter turn each week or it leans towards the light.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Boston Blue Bell'
plants.tip: Copes with ordinary rooms better than most, but it still drops fronds if it dries out completely.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Piersonii'
plants.tip: An old, heavy cultivar for a basket. Soak the pot in a sink rather than dribbling water on top.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Mini Russells'
plants.tip: Tiny pots dry within days. Sit it in a shallow tray of water for ten minutes, then let it drain.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Mini Ruffle'
plants.tip: Small and slow. Feed monthly at half strength in summer; a full dose burns the fine roots.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Silver Balls'
plants.tip: Compact and dense. Runners creep over the rim and can be pegged into a second pot to root.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Montana'
plants.tip: Keep it clear of draughts from a door or radiator. Dry moving air crisps the frond tips first.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Petticoat'
plants.tip: Frilled fronds hold water in the crown. Water in the morning so it is not sitting wet overnight.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Vitale'
plants.tip: Upright and tidy, so brown tips show plainly. Those are dry air, not a watering fault.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Sonata'
plants.tip: Even moisture is the whole job. Compost that swings between soaked and bone dry sheds fronds.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Marisa'
plants.tip: Short lacy fronds in a small pot. Judge by the weight of the pot, not the look of the compost.

plants.name: Nephrolepis exaltata 'Todeoides'
plants.tip: Long arching fronds want room. A cramped spot snaps them, and a broken frond does not regrow.

plants.name: Nephrolepis cordifolia (fishbone fern)
plants.tip: Underground tubers store water, so it forgives a missed watering that would set a Boston fern back.

plants.name: Nephrolepis cordifolia 'Duffii' (lemon button fern)
plants.tip: The round buttons take drier air than most ferns, but not a fully dry rootball.

plants.name: Nephrolepis cordifolia 'Plumosa' (dwarf Whitman fern)
plants.tip: Feathery and compact. Cut the old fronds at the base in spring to make room for the new flush.

plants.name: Nephrolepis biserrata (giant sword fern)
plants.tip: It gets large. Give it a heavy pot and floor space, and keep the compost damp right through summer.

plants.name: Nephrolepis biserrata 'Macho' (macho fern)
plants.tip: Grows to about a metre across. Water deeply and let only the surface dry, never the whole rootball.

plants.name: Nephrolepis biserrata 'Furcans' (fishtail fern)
plants.tip: The forked frond tips are the point of it, and direct sun scorches them first. Keep it in shade.
